title: the bell jar - sylvia plath
body:
preface

hiiiiiiii i have decided no time is better than right now to reacquaint myself with reading. it really does feel like the natural evolution of everything that interests me currently. 

im starting with the bell jar because A it is critically acclaimed B i own it C i did not fully read it when i bought it 3 years ago

i do not know much about this book, from what i remember it is about a woman who goes to school in new york and her experience with that life? i know it is a sorrowful book. the cover itself fills me with so much dread.

i think the way im going to operate this is similar to evangelion, ill write notes down during a chapter, and after each chapter ill do a small recap of everything that i know. gonna start reading now!

**chapter 1**

"the summer they electrocuted the rosenbergs"
-a couple convicted of being soviet spies, executed by electric chair
-1953

"i couldnt help wondering what it would be like, being burned alive along all your nerves"

dislikes new york, describes it similarly to how one would describe hell

buddy willard (fictional) showed narrator a cadaver that burned an image into her mind at some point in life, she compares the talk of the rosenburgs to how the cadaver haunted her

"Only I wasn't steering anything, not even myself."

she won a fashion magazine contest along with 11 other girls who were all flown out to new york to essentially be dunked into the high end fashion culture for free

she describes the makeup kit they gave her, made tailored for her, as a kit for a person with brown eyes and brown hair. she doesnt say my brown eyes and my brown hair. just a person. devaluation of herself?

the narrator is recounting her own events from this month, she has a child now. she also says she hid the things she was gifted for a while, foreshadowing bad memories associated with this time

there is a weird dynamic of the narrator both viewing herself as above the girls who lived at this hotel with her, while also being jealous of them

im almost immediately picking up on this sense of doreen being the antithesis of the narrator similar to asuka/rei. doreen is fully happy and living in the material world, while the narrator is in a completely different headspace, though she wants to be able to come back down to the material world i believe

"i always had a terribly hard time trying to imagine people in bed together"
-asexual?

"Doreen had intuition. Everything she said was like a secret voice speaking straight out of my own bones."
-gonna watch how doreen develops very carefully

"being with Doreen made me forget my worries. I felt wise and cynical as all hell"
-she wants to be doreen or she is in love with doreen?

narrator has described the last 2 men both having something to do with the color blue. maybe coincidence but figure id put it down so i remember if it happens again

Buddy Willard was a medical student at the college narrator attended

"my dream was someday ordering a drink and finding out it tasted wonderful"
-seemingly insignificant but i think this shows some lack of agency, why else point it out? actually, as a i type this, i think its more that she's so hyper-aware of herself that she won't even ask what a good drink is, she thinks that will embarrass her so instead she suffers and gambles on what she drinks. 

she describes another man as wearing blue!, the short friend of frankie

"even when they surprised me or made me sick I never let on, but pretended that's the way I knew things were all the time."

post chapter:

the narrator (who we still dont know the name of, ill call her elly for now) seems to have the worst case of scared-of-being-acknowledged-ism that i have ever witnessed. i get her though. i think i very much used to do similar. she gives a fake name to frankie, she doesnt outwardly express her feelings, shes ashamed of where she came from, she admits to pretending she always knew things even if she just learned them.

as i typed the above I also realized the reason we may not know her name yet is because she views herself as so unimportant and is so terrified of being recognized that she won't even admit to something as menial as that in her own story.

there's obviously some connection between elly and doreen, doreen is the outgoing, confident, present girl that elly wishes she could be; doreen does not despise this difference though, elly even says she was singled out. doreen may just see a good friend in elly, while elly thinks shes being picked as a charity case

**chapter 2**
